sources.register_note: Reconstructed from ONS totals (£2,498bn of gilts, 24% index-linked, average maturity 13y conventional / 17y linkers); conventional coupon 2.64% calibrated to the £66.2bn of interest the ONS recorded in the last complete year. Upload the DMO gilts-in-issue (D1A) report for the gilt-by-gilt version.

rules.name: Stability rule
rules.description: Current budget (receipts less day-to-day spending, including debt interest) in balance or surplus in the target year. Headroom = current budget surplus, £bn.

rules.name: Investment rule
rules.description: Public sector net financial liabilities falling as a share of GDP in the target year. Headroom = fall in the ratio, shown in £bn at that year's GDP.

scenarios.name: Rates +100bp
scenarios.description: Bank Rate and gilt yields 1pp higher for good from next year.

scenarios.name: Gilt term-premium shock
scenarios.description: Gilt yields 1.5pp higher with an unchanged Bank Rate (a fiscal risk premium).

scenarios.name: Recession
scenarios.description: Real growth 2pp lower for two years; automatic stabilisers widen the deficit.

scenarios.name: Inflation shock
scenarios.description: Inflation 3pp higher for two years, Bank Rate 1.5pp and gilts 1pp higher in response.

scenarios.name: 2022 replay
scenarios.description: As in 2022–23: inflation up 6pp then 3pp, Bank Rate up 3pp, gilts up 2.5pp, growth 1pp lower.

scenarios.name: 2008 replay
scenarios.description: As in 2008–10: growth 5pp lower then 1pp, deficit 3% of GDP wider for three years, Bank Rate cut 3pp.

scenarios.name: Combined adverse
scenarios.description: Recession plus a gilt risk premium: growth 1.5pp lower for two years, gilts 1.5pp and Bank Rate 1pp higher.

cyclical.note: Semi-elasticity of the primary balance to the output gap (OBR cyclical adjustment is about 0.5–0.6) and output-gap persistence.

issuance_mix.note: Assumed split of gross financing (a typical recent DMO remit); edit to match the current remit.

apf.note: OBR March 2026 assumption: £65bn a year reduction in the APF (redemptions plus £32bn of active sales).

model.rules_note: Both rules are assessed in 2029-30 until it becomes the third year of the forecast, then in the third year (rolling). Since the November 2025 Budget the OBR formally assesses the rules once a year, at the Budget.
model.extension_note: Years after the OBR horizon: real growth, GDP deflator and primary balance held at the OBR's final year; rates from the market curves.
